tip.title: Same, or opposite?
tip.text: SYNONYMS are words with almost the same meaning (big / large / huge). ANTONYMS are opposites (big / small). Writers switch between synonyms so the text does not repeat. When a question asks for a word that means the same, swap it into the sentence and check that the sentence still makes sense.

passage.title: Battle of Words
passage.text:
A rap battle is a contest of words. Two rappers face each other on a stage. Each one gets a turn to attack the other with rhymes. The crowd decides who was sharper, faster, and funnier.

In the Philippines, rap battles became huge after 2010, when leagues started posting videos online. Some battles have been watched tens of millions of times. The best battlers are not just quick. They are clever. They play with words, twist meanings, and set up jokes three lines before the punchline.

Battlers prepare for weeks. They study their opponent, write hundreds of lines, and cut the weak ones. On stage, though, the strongest moment is often a comeback made up on the spot.

Teachers have noticed something. Students who follow battle rap learn new words fast. They hear a word in a verse, look it up, and use it. A rapper who wants to win must have a big vocabulary. So must a student who wants to read well. The battle is the same; only the stage is different.

words.example: She shook hands with her opponent after the match.

words.meaning: smart in a quick, creative way
words.example: That was a clever way to solve the puzzle.

words.meaning: all the words a person knows and uses

items.prompt: Which word means almost the SAME as huge?
items.why: Huge and enormous both mean very big. "Rap battles became enormous after 2010" keeps the meaning.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of sharp (as used for a rapper)?
items.why: Sharp means quick and clever. Dull is its opposite. The other choices are synonyms of sharp.

items.prompt: "They cut the weak ones." Which word means the same as weak here?
items.why: Weak lines are poor lines. "They cut the poor ones" keeps the meaning.

items.prompt: Which pair of words from the passage are synonyms?
items.why: A contest and a battle are both competitions. The passage calls a rap battle "a contest of words."

items.prompt: What is the main idea of the LAST paragraph?
choices: Following battle rap builds vocabulary, which is the same skill reading needs.
items.why: The paragraph connects rap vocabulary to reading vocabulary: "The battle is the same; only the stage is different."

items.prompt: Why did rap battles become popular in the Philippines after 2010?
items.why: "Rap battles became huge after 2010, when leagues started posting videos online."
